title: My Favorite Part of the New Kindle Paperwhite Is One of the Accessories
gist: Wired reviews the 2026 Kindle Paperwhite and Colorsoft (8/10): minimal hardware changes, prices held after Amazon raised 2024 models in August, colors locked to Signature Editions, and an $80 Page Turn Cover as the most compelling extra.

insights.claim: The 2026 Kindle Paperwhite and Colorsoft cost the same as the 2024 editions only because Amazon raised prices on the 2024 versions in August, making new models feel worth buying.
insights.speaker: Nena Farrell
insights.so_what: Price anchoring by hiking old models is a lever for steering buyers to new SKUs.
insights.locator: It's worth noting that while the price

insights.claim: Prices are $200 for Paperwhite, $250 for Paperwhite Signature, $290 for Colorsoft, and $320 for Colorsoft Signature.
insights.speaker: Nena Farrell
insights.so_what: Reference pricing for the 2026 Kindle line.

insights.claim: Colored finishes are now limited to Signature Editions, one color per model, while base 7-inch models come only in black.
insights.speaker: Nena Farrell
insights.so_what: Color is used as an upsell driver, which Amazon says motivated upgrades after 2024's colors.

themes.theme: Accessories as a hedge on demand

insights.claim: Amazon says only about 5 percent of Kindle users want page-turn buttons, so it made them an $80 add-on (Page Turn Cover) rather than building them into a device, which the reviewer calls a smart move.
insights.speaker: Nena Farrell
insights.so_what: Accessory strategy lets Amazon serve niche demand without SKU risk, but raises total cost of ownership.
insights.quote: Amazon says it's a vocal minority of about 5 percent of Kindle users

insights.claim: The cheapest combination for page-turn buttons, Paperwhite Signature plus the cover, exceeds $300, which is what the Kobo Libra Colour costs with built-in buttons and a stylus.
insights.speaker: Nena Farrell
insights.so_what: Kobo is price-competitive for feature-rich e-readers.

insights.claim: The $35 Bluetooth Kindle Click remote works with Kindles from 2024 onward and is a much cheaper alternative to the cover.
insights.speaker: Nena Farrell
insights.so_what: Cheap accessory extends older devices' life, reducing urgency to upgrade.

insights.claim: Specs are largely unchanged: 7.2 ounces versus 7.4 or 7.6 before, 300 ppi black-and-white and 150 ppi color, up to 12 weeks (Paperwhite) and eight (Colorsoft) of battery life, and no meaningful speed gain.
insights.speaker: Nena Farrell
insights.so_what: Incremental refresh; upgrade case is weak for existing owners.

insights.claim: New Kindles add AI features: Recap (Story So Far) gives spoiler-free summaries based on reading progress, and Ask This Book is promised as coming soon; the reviewer does not expect to use them.
insights.speaker: Nena Farrell
insights.so_what: Amazon is embedding LLM features into e-readers as a differentiator, but user appeal is questionable.

insights.claim: E Ink announced a new version of its color e-paper screen, but the reviewer does not expect it in devices until next year at the earliest.
insights.speaker: Nena Farrell
insights.so_what: Next color e-paper generation is the likelier driver for a real Colorsoft upgrade cycle.
